title: Découverte des sons autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify and reproduce simple environmental sounds using their voice

opening.activity: Sound exploration circle - teacher makes different environmental sounds (wind, rain, birds) and students guess and imitate
opening.visualSupports: TPR gestures for 'écouter' (cup ear), pictures of sound sources, exaggerated facial expressions for different sounds

main.activity: Sound safari around the classroom and school - students listen for sounds and practice reproducing them with their voice, creating a class sound map
main.visualSupports: Visual sound map on wall, hand signals for loud/quiet, mouth shape demonstrations for different sounds

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable making sounds in French or still in silent period?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage more complex sound combinations and introduce French sound words
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue modeling and allow pointing/gesturing, celebrate any vocal attempts

decisionPoints.question: Do students recognize the difference between loud and soft sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Add volume variation games and introduce 'fort' and 'doucement'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on clear modeling of volume differences with exaggerated gestures

closing.activity: Circle reflection - each student shares one favorite sound from today using voice or gesture
closing.assessment: Observe student comfort level with vocal expression and sound recognition

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students reluctant to make sounds aloud
troubleshooting.then: Start with whisper sounds, use puppet to demonstrate, create safe 'quiet practice' space

realWorldConnection: Connecting to sounds they hear at home, playground, and in nature

title: Mon corps fait de la musique
oneGoal: Students will create rhythms using body percussion (clapping, tapping, stomping)

opening.activity: Body part warm-up song - teacher leads simple movements naming body parts used for making rhythm
opening.visualSupports: Large body diagram poster, teacher modeling clear movements, rhythm pattern cards with pictures

main.activity: Body percussion orchestra - students explore different body sounds (clap, pat, stomp, snap) then combine into simple patterns
main.visualSupports: Conductor gestures, visual rhythm patterns (long/short lines), body movement demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to maintain a steady beat with their bodies?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce more complex patterns and combination movements
decisionPoints.ifNo: Return to single steady beat practice with music support

decisionPoints.question: Should I introduce call-and-response patterns now?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start simple 2-beat call and response games
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with unison pattern practice to build confidence

closing.activity: Body rhythm performance - students choose their favorite body percussion sound to share with the class
closing.assessment: Check if students can maintain steady beat and coordinate movements

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students losing steady beat or coordination
troubleshooting.then: Slow down tempo, use strong musical backing, practice one movement at a time

realWorldConnection: Like clapping along to favorite songs or marching like soldiers

title: Les animaux chantent aussi
oneGoal: Students will imitate animal sounds with different vocal expressions and rhythms

opening.activity: Animal sound guessing game - teacher makes animal sounds and students guess the animal, then practice together
opening.visualSupports: Large animal pictures, mouth shape demonstrations for each sound, animal movement gestures

main.activity: Animal rhythm parade - students choose an animal, learn its French sound, create a rhythm pattern, then parade around classroom
main.visualSupports: Animal movement demonstrations, rhythm pattern charts for each animal, visual parade route map

decisionPoints.question: Are students connecting animal sounds to rhythm patterns?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to create longer patterns or combine two animals
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on one animal sound at a time before adding rhythm element

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on fewer animals for deeper exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose 3-4 animals and develop complex rhythms and movements
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with variety to maintain engagement and choice

closing.activity: Animal orchestra - all students perform their animal sounds and rhythms together, then in small groups
closing.assessment: Observe vocal variety and rhythm integration in animal sounds

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students making sounds too quietly or without rhythm
troubleshooting.then: Use animal puppets for confidence, exaggerate movements, practice volume control games

realWorldConnection: Connecting to pets, farm animals, or zoo animals they know

title: Répéter comme un écho
oneGoal: Students will echo simple sound and rhythm patterns with increasing accuracy

opening.activity: Echo mountain story - teacher tells simple story about mountain echoes while demonstrating echo patterns
opening.visualSupports: Mountain landscape visual, hand gestures for sound traveling, echo ripple movements

main.activity: Echo challenge games - teacher creates patterns of increasing complexity, students echo back, then students become echo leaders
main.visualSupports: Visual pattern representation, conductor gestures, turn-taking cards for student leaders

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for 3-4 beat patterns or should I stick to 2 beats?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Gradually increase to 3-4 beat patterns with visual support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Master 2-beat patterns thoroughly before progression

decisionPoints.question: Should I add visual cues to support the auditory patterns?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use hand movements or visual cards to represent each beat
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with purely auditory challenge to develop listening skills

closing.activity: Echo circle - students sit in circle and each creates an echo pattern for the next person to repeat
closing.assessment: Check accuracy of pattern reproduction and listening attention

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not hearing or remembering patterns accurately
troubleshooting.then: Slow down tempo, add visual cues, start with shorter patterns, use familiar songs

realWorldConnection: Like echoing in mountains or repeating after parents

title: Mes premiers mots rythmés
oneGoal: Students will clap the syllables in their own names and simple French words

opening.activity: Name clapping circle - each student claps their name while saying it, class echoes back
opening.visualSupports: Name cards with dots showing syllables, hand clapping demonstrations, syllable counting fingers

main.activity: Word rhythm workshop - students practice clapping syllables in family words, classroom objects, then create word rhythm chains
main.visualSupports: Picture cards with syllable divisions marked, counting fingers for each syllable, rhythm chain visual map

decisionPoints.question: Can students hear the beats in their names clearly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Move to more complex French vocabulary and compound words
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with names and very familiar words, add more physical movement

decisionPoints.question: Should I use visual syllable counting to support understanding?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide counting mats and visual syllable representations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on auditory and kinesthetic learning through movement

closing.activity: Syllable symphony - students perform their favorite word rhythms as a class orchestra
closing.assessment: Observe accuracy of syllable counting and rhythm coordination

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty hearing syllables in words
troubleshooting.then: Use chin-drop method, exaggerate pronunciation, start with two-syllable words only

realWorldConnection: Their own names and words for family members they use daily

title: Comptines simples et mouvements
oneGoal: Students will participate in a simple French nursery rhyme with coordinated movements

opening.activity: Nursery rhyme introduction - teacher shares a simple French comptine with actions, students watch and listen
opening.visualSupports: Large illustrated comptine poster, clear action demonstrations, picture sequence cards

main.activity: Learn 'Frère Jacques' with movements - break down rhyme line by line, add simple actions, practice together
main.visualSupports: Line-by-line poster breakdown, action demonstrations, musical notation for rhythm

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for full participation or need more listening time?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage singing along and creating own action variations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue modeling and allow students to join in gradually

decisionPoints.question: Should I simplify movements to focus on rhythm or add complexity?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Add more complex movements and rhythm variations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep movements simple and focus on staying with the beat

closing.activity: Performance circle - students perform comptine with actions, celebrating participation over perfection
closing.assessment: Check coordination of words, rhythm, and movement integration

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by combining words, rhythm, and movement
troubleshooting.then: Break into separate components, practice rhythm only first, then add elements gradually

realWorldConnection: Like singing games they play with siblings or at daycare

title: Inventer des rythmes ensemble
oneGoal: Students will collaborate to create original rhythm patterns using voice and body

opening.activity: Collaboration warm-up - pairs practice copying each other's simple movements and sounds
opening.visualSupports: Partner work visual rules, turn-taking signals, collaboration gesture demonstrations

main.activity: Rhythm invention station - small groups create original patterns using voice, body percussion, and simple instruments
main.visualSupports: Creation process poster, collaboration roles chart, rhythm notation examples

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable taking creative risks in French?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage more experimental sounds and complex pattern creation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more structure and sentence starters for creative expression

decisionPoints.question: Should I guide the collaboration more directly or let them lead?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Step back and observe, intervene only when needed
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more structured roles and step-by-step collaboration process

closing.activity: Rhythm gallery walk - groups share their created patterns, others appreciate and echo back
closing.assessment: Observe creative collaboration and willingness to share original work

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Groups having difficulty collaborating or creating together
troubleshooting.then: Assign specific roles, provide creation templates, model collaboration process

realWorldConnection: Like making up games or songs with friends during play

title: Émotions dans ma voix
oneGoal: Students will express different emotions through vocal tone while maintaining rhythm

opening.activity: Emotion demonstration - teacher shows how voice changes with different feelings using simple sounds
opening.visualSupports: Large emotion face posters, facial expression demonstrations, voice pitch visual representations

main.activity: Emotional rhythm theater - students practice saying simple phrases with different emotions while clapping steady beat
main.visualSupports: Emotion-phrase combination chart, vocal expression demonstrations, rhythm pattern guides

decisionPoints.question: Can students differentiate emotions in vocal expression clearly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Add more subtle emotions and complex phrases
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on clear contrasts (happy/sad, loud/quiet) with exaggerated modeling

decisionPoints.question: Should I model more extensively or encourage immediate practice?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage student experimentation with support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more modeling and guided practice before independent work

closing.activity: Emotion rhythm circle - students share how their voice sounds when they feel different emotions
closing.assessment: Check ability to vary vocal expression while maintaining rhythmic structure

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty changing vocal expression
troubleshooting.then: Use puppets to practice, exaggerate facial expressions, practice with familiar songs

realWorldConnection: How their voice changes when happy, sad, or excited at home

title: Rimes qui résonnent
oneGoal: Students will identify and create simple rhyming sounds in French

opening.activity: Rhyme detective game - teacher says pairs of words, students identify which ones rhyme
opening.visualSupports: Rhyming word picture pairs, visual rhyme identification signals, word ending emphasis demonstrations

main.activity: Rhyme creation workshop - students work with word families to create new rhyming combinations and simple verses
main.visualSupports: Word family posters, rhyme pattern demonstrations, creation process chart

decisionPoints.question: Do students hear the similar ending sounds in rhymes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Move to creating original rhymes and longer rhyming sequences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with identification games and exaggerated pronunciation practice

decisionPoints.question: Are they ready to generate rhymes or need more identification practice?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage original rhyme creation with simple word families
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue identification activities with more word examples

closing.activity: Rhyme sharing circle - students share their favorite rhyming word pair or creation
closing.assessment: Observe rhyme recognition and beginning generative rhyming ability

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not hearing similar ending sounds
troubleshooting.then: Exaggerate word endings, use visual word cards, practice with body movements for each sound

realWorldConnection: Like silly word games and rhyming songs they hear in French media

title: Tempo: vite et lentement
oneGoal: Students will perform the same rhythm pattern at different speeds with control

opening.activity: Speed demonstration - teacher walks, then runs, showing how same movement changes with tempo
opening.visualSupports: Speed demonstration movements, tempo visual indicators, fast/slow comparison posters

main.activity: Tempo control challenge - students practice familiar rhythm patterns at different speeds, playing tempo games
main.visualSupports: Tempo speed indicators, conductor gestures for speed changes, visual rhythm representations

decisionPoints.question: Can students maintain rhythm accuracy when changing speed?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Add more dramatic tempo changes and complex patterns
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on gradual tempo changes with simpler patterns

decisionPoints.question: Should I add instrumental support or keep it vocal/body only?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce simple percussion to support tempo control
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue developing internal tempo control with voice and body

closing.activity: Tempo performance - students demonstrate their control by performing same pattern fast and slow
closing.assessment: Check tempo control and rhythm accuracy at different speeds

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students losing rhythm accuracy when changing tempo
troubleshooting.then: Use strong musical backing, practice tempo changes very gradually, focus on steady beat first

realWorldConnection: Like walking slowly or running fast, or songs that speed up and slow down

title: Ma première performance
oneGoal: Students will perform a simple rhythm and rhyme combination for classmates

opening.activity: Performance preparation circle - discuss what makes a good audience and performer
opening.visualSupports: Good audience behavior demonstrations, performer confidence gestures, applause signals

main.activity: Performance preparation and sharing - students choose and rehearse their performance, then share with small groups
main.visualSupports: Performance checklist, rehearsal process chart, confidence-building affirmations poster

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to perform individually or need partner support?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage individual performances with supportive audience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Allow partner or small group performances for confidence

decisionPoints.question: Do they need more rehearsal time or are they confident to share?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Proceed with performances and celebrate attempts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more rehearsal time and confidence-building activities

closing.activity: Celebration circle - appreciate all performances and discuss what they learned about performing
closing.assessment: Observe confidence in performance and application of rhythm/rhyme skills

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too nervous or reluctant to perform
troubleshooting.then: Start with partner performances, use props for confidence, create very supportive audience atmosphere

realWorldConnection: Like showing family a new song or dance they learned

title: Jouer avec les mots drôles
oneGoal: Students will create and share silly word combinations that maintain rhyme and rhythm

opening.activity: Silly word warm-up - teacher demonstrates funny nonsense words with exaggerated expressions
opening.visualSupports: Exaggerated facial expressions, silly sound demonstrations, humor encouragement posters

main.activity: Nonsense word creation lab - students invent silly words that rhyme and create funny rhythm patterns
main.visualSupports: Word creation process chart, rhyme pattern guides, humor celebration indicators

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable being playful with French language?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage more creative and experimental word combinations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with simple modifications of familiar words, celebrate any attempts

decisionPoints.question: Do they need prompts for silly ideas or are they generating freely?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let creativity flow with minimal guidance
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide silly word stems and rhyming partners to spark ideas

closing.activity: Silly word showcase - students share their funniest creations and the class enjoys the humor together
closing.assessment: Check creative language use and maintenance of rhyme/rhythm structure

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students being too serious or worried about 'correct' French
troubleshooting.then: Model more silliness, emphasize that mistakes are fun, use humor games to build comfort

realWorldConnection: Like making up funny words or nonsense songs for entertainment

title: Raconter avec le rythme
oneGoal: Students will tell a simple story using rhythmic speech patterns

opening.activity: Rhythmic storytelling demonstration - teacher tells familiar story with strong rhythm and beat
opening.visualSupports: Story sequence pictures, rhythm emphasis demonstrations, storytelling gesture guides

main.activity: Rhythmic story creation - students choose simple story elements and practice telling with rhythm emphasis
main.visualSupports: Story structure charts, rhythm pattern overlays, narrative flow indicators

decisionPoints.question: Can students maintain story coherence while focusing on rhythm?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage longer stories and more complex rhythmic patterns
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on very simple stories with repetitive rhythmic elements

decisionPoints.question: Should I emphasize rhythm or storytelling as the primary focus?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both elements with equal emphasis
decisionPoints.ifNo: Choose primary focus based on student needs and comfort level

closing.activity: Story rhythm sharing - students share their rhythmic stories in small groups or with partners
closing.assessment: Observe integration of narrative structure with rhythmic speech patterns

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students losing story thread when focusing on rhythm
troubleshooting.then: Use story picture supports, practice rhythm with familiar stories first, allow simpler narratives

realWorldConnection: Like telling exciting stories with dramatic voices to friends or family

title: Célébrer nos créations
oneGoal: Students will self-assess their growth in rhythm and rhyme while celebrating peer achievements

opening.activity: Growth reflection warm-up - students think about what they could do at the beginning vs. now
opening.visualSupports: Growth visualization charts, progress celebration indicators, achievement recognition symbols

main.activity: Achievement gallery walk - students showcase their best work and provide positive feedback to peers
main.visualSupports: Achievement display areas, feedback sentence starters, celebration ritual demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Can students articulate what they've learned in French?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage detailed reflections and goal-setting for future
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide sentence starters and visual prompts for reflection

decisionPoints.question: Are they able to give constructive feedback to peers?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow more independent peer feedback and appreciation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide structured feedback templates and model positive language

closing.activity: Celebration circle - each student shares one thing they're proud of learning
closing.assessment: Check student ability to self-reflect and recognize their own growth

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty recognizing their own progress
troubleshooting.then: Provide specific examples of their growth, use video/audio recordings to show change

realWorldConnection: Like family celebrations of learning to ride a bike or tie shoes

title: Partager notre musicalité
oneGoal: Students will present their favorite rhythm and rhyme creation to a wider audience

opening.activity: Audience preparation - discuss how to share their learning with others outside the classroom
opening.visualSupports: Presentation structure charts, audience engagement tips, confidence-building reminders

main.activity: Final presentation preparation and performance - students finalize and present their chosen pieces
main.visualSupports: Performance setup guides, presentation structure reminders, celebration protocols

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for a larger audience or need more preparation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Invite other classes or family members to attend
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep audience small and very supportive

decisionPoints.question: Should presentations be individual or can they work in groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow both individual and group presentations based on preference
decisionPoints.ifNo: Choose format based on student comfort and learning goals

closing.activity: Appreciation and reflection - audience provides feedback and students reflect on sharing experience
closing.assessment: Observe confidence in presentation and application of all learned skills

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by larger audience or presentation pressure
troubleshooting.then: Reduce audience size, allow partner support, focus on celebration over perfection

realWorldConnection: Like school concerts or sharing talents at family gatherings

title: Rythmes du monde francophone
oneGoal: Students will explore rhythm patterns from different French-speaking cultures

opening.activity: Francophone world introduction - show map and listen to rhythm samples from different countries
opening.visualSupports: Large francophone world map, cultural rhythm visual representations, country identification pictures

main.activity: Cultural rhythm exploration stations - students experience rhythms from Quebec, Senegal, and France
main.visualSupports: Cultural rhythm pattern charts, instrument demonstrations, geographical connection visuals

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to distinguish between different cultural rhythm styles?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore more subtle differences and cultural context
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on clear contrasts and repetitive practice with each style

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on one culture deeply or survey several briefly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose one culture for deep exploration this lesson
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with variety to expose students to diversity

closing.activity: Cultural rhythm appreciation - students share which rhythm style they enjoyed most and why
closing.assessment: Check ability to distinguish cultural rhythm styles and cultural awareness

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused by cultural differences or overwhelmed by variety
troubleshooting.then: Focus on similarities first, use visual and geographical supports, emphasize appreciation over analysis

realWorldConnection: Connecting to diverse music they might hear in their multicultural community

title: Poésie et nature
oneGoal: Students will create nature-inspired poems using environmental sounds and rhythms

opening.activity: Nature sound meditation - listen to winter nature sounds and discuss rhythms in nature
opening.visualSupports: Winter nature photographs, sound wave representations, seasonal rhythm demonstrations

main.activity: Nature poetry creation - students observe winter elements and create simple poems with natural rhythms
main.visualSupports: Poetry structure examples, nature rhythm patterns, seasonal vocabulary pictures

decisionPoints.question: Can students connect natural phenomena to rhythmic patterns?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage more complex nature observations and poetic structures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple nature sounds and basic rhythmic connections

decisionPoints.question: Should we go outside for inspiration or use indoor imagination?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Take brief outdoor observation time if weather permits
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use classroom nature materials and imagination activities

closing.activity: Nature poetry sharing - students share their nature poems with natural rhythm patterns
closing.assessment: Observe connection between natural observations and poetic rhythm creation

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty connecting nature to rhythm or poetry
troubleshooting.then: Use more concrete examples, provide nature rhythm templates, focus on familiar nature experiences

realWorldConnection: Observing winter weather, birds, and seasonal changes around them

title: Instruments et voix ensemble
oneGoal: Students will combine simple percussion instruments with vocal rhythms

opening.activity: Instrument and voice demonstration - teacher shows how instruments can support and enhance voice
opening.visualSupports: Instrument demonstration visuals, voice-instrument coordination guides, sound combination charts

main.activity: Voice-instrument orchestra - students practice coordinating their voice with instruments in small groups
main.visualSupports: Coordination pattern guides, group work structure charts, conductor signal demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Can students coordinate instrumental and vocal elements simultaneously?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Add more complex coordination patterns and independence
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on alternating voice and instrument rather than simultaneous coordination

decisionPoints.question: Should I limit instrument choices or offer full variety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide full variety for exploration and choice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Limit to 2-3 instruments to focus coordination skills

closing.activity: Mixed ensemble performance - groups perform their voice-instrument combinations for each other
closing.assessment: Check coordination of vocal and instrumental elements and ensemble cooperation

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by coordinating voice and instrument simultaneously
troubleshooting.then: Practice each element separately first, use turn-taking instead of simultaneous coordination

realWorldConnection: Like family music time or joining in with recorded songs using objects

title: Créer un spectacle de classe
oneGoal: Students will collaborate to design and rehearse a class rhythm and poetry showcase

opening.activity: Showcase planning circle - discuss what elements to include in their class performance
opening.visualSupports: Showcase structure examples, collaboration process charts, planning timeline visuals

main.activity: Collaborative showcase creation - students work in groups to plan and rehearse showcase elements
main.visualSupports: Showcase planning guides, group work structure charts, rehearsal process timelines

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to work independently in planning groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow more autonomous group work with periodic check-ins
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more structured guidance and step-by-step planning support

decisionPoints.question: Should I assign roles or let them negotiate responsibilities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let students negotiate with conflict resolution support available
decisionPoints.ifNo: Assign clear roles to ensure all students have meaningful participation

closing.activity: Showcase preview - groups share their plans and get feedback from other groups
closing.assessment: Observe collaborative planning skills and integration of learned rhythm/poetry elements

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Groups having conflict or difficulty making decisions together
troubleshooting.then: Provide conflict resolution strategies, assign specific roles, break into smaller planning steps

realWorldConnection: Like organizing family talent shows or community celebrations

title: Notre héritage rythmique
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their growth and plan how to continue using rhythm and poetry in daily life

opening.activity: Learning journey reflection - students look back at their work from lesson 1 to now
opening.visualSupports: Learning journey timeline, growth comparison charts, achievement celebration displays

main.activity: Future planning and legacy creation - students plan how to use their skills and create a class rhythm legacy
main.visualSupports: Future planning guides, goal visualization charts, legacy project examples

decisionPoints.question: Can students articulate specific ways they'll use these skills outside class?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage detailed planning and specific goal-setting
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide concrete examples and guided reflection questions

decisionPoints.question: Do they understand the connection between rhythm and language learning?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore deeper connections and advanced applications
decisionPoints.ifNo: Make explicit connections with examples and demonstrations

closing.activity: Legacy celebration - students share their plans and celebrate their rhythm and poetry journey
closing.assessment: Check understanding of learning transfer and commitment to continued rhythm/poetry use

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students unable to see connections to future learning or daily life
troubleshooting.then: Provide concrete examples, connect to family experiences, use visual planning supports

realWorldConnection: Planning to share skills with family and use rhythm to help with French learning
